questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had been wanting to learn/study Catalan for a long time, while also wanting to improve my Spanish, so the language aspects that Barcelona offers were definitely crucial.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was still quite messy unfortunately and not always so transparent as to where to find the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a very brief introduction meeting, but it didn´t include any new information if you had read the welcome email, so I was a bit disappointed by that. It must be said though, that the local coordinators were very welcoming and tried their best to answer questions if you came to them.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very hard to find (affordable) housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Barcelona I haven´t heard of any "on campus" housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After confirming our courses, we had to wait around a week until we were enrolled and received the login details.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The coordinators from the international office for incoming students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One of my five courses was too full, which meant I had to change to a different course. For two other courses I changed after a week due to own mistakes (clashing schedules and accidentally choosing a course taught in Catalan).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To look carefully at the teaching languages for the courses and if choosing courses from different faculties, to check when the individual faculties start their classes because it might differ from faculty to faculty.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two courses for first year BA students and three courses for third or fourth year BA students (as the BA in Spain is 4 years).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was much more one-sided at UB compared to UPCH, meaning that the leactures mostly consisted of the professors talking and not a lot of discussions and class participation. We were mostly fed information and not encouraged to come to our own conclusions and reflect on the new knowledge.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introducción a la historia de la lengua española (6 ECTS)
Introducción a la literatura hispanoamericana (6 ECTS)
Traducció desde l´Alemany (6 ECTS)
Literatura i Holocaust (6 ECTS)
Enseñanza del Inglés como Lengua Extranjera I (6 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
To students who a very proficient in Spanish I would recommend Introducción a la historia de la lengua española, although it it also a very intense course.
For German speaking students or simply students interested in German history or just literature, I will recommend Literatura i Holocaust, which was my favourite subject this semester and is taught by a wonderful professor. The downside is that it involves a lot of reading (three novels plus other texts), but the way the class is taught resembles UCPH more than most other classes.

questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The public transportation was very good and much cheaper than anticipated. The T-Jove card valid for 90 days for ca. 300DKK including all 6 zones of Barcelona.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I participated in the CATclub (Catalan Club) who organise weekly activities for students who want to learn Catalan and about Catalan culture and history. There is also a UB sports organisation, which I initially wanted to sign up for to play volleyball, but it was extremely intransparent and in the end I didn´t join the sports club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I will definitely recommend joing the CATclub. It was a great way to learn Catalan and an amazing opportunity to learn about Catalan customs with both Catalans and internationals and you get to do things and visit places that you probably would´nt have the opportunity to as a "normal" exchange student.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I can highly recommend playing volleyball at the beach in Barcelona and also to make use of the transportation card and visit nearby beaches and towns. Barcelona also has great museums and cultural sites and there are many ways to enjoy them for free om certain days.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I felt that because the situation with tourists in Barcelona is very complicated right now, I wasn´t always welcome , even though I was an exchange student and not a tourist. But I often felt (with neighbours, people at the beach, etc.) that this difference didn´t matter and even though I speak Spanish and now also Catalan, that I was judged very quickly and constantly felt the need to prove that I wasn´t like "those other tourists".

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Definitely try to at least learn a little bit of Catalan. The Catalan identity is very strong, and combined with the growing resentment towards tourists in Barcelona, many local people are not too happy to hear English or sometimes even Spanish/Castellano spoken to them. Speaking Catalan to local people has been a gamechanger for me, as people are instantly more friendly and open and can see that you are making an effort.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The perception of time and what is considered being late, as I have often had to wait for people I had agreed to meet with and still struggle to get used to people not showing up on time (what I consider to be on time).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The spontaneity.
I also really like how protective Catalan people can be of their language and the effort they make to maintain it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don´t underestimate the role the Catalan language plays here. Don´t come there and expect everyone to speak Spanish with you or that most things will be in Spanish (let alone English).
2. In most cases, for example when you are unsure about exams, grades etc., you can ask your professors - don´t be shy!
3. Join the CATclub activites! It was really one of my highlights.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The historical building of the UB is very beautiful and definitely worth a visit - and the library there is amaying and much nicer for studzing than the ones at other UB campuses.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people that I met and the friendships I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Paper work, problems with our landlord and apartment.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
